mainTopic: Fixing the wording of רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה (טועות instead of שוטות), and a ברייתא that shows how a woman with a regular, predictable bleeding pattern figures out which days she may be with her husband.
overview: The גמרא first fixes a word in רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה. Women who are unsure of their cycle are 'mistaken' (טועות), not 'foolish' (שוטות). It then quotes a ברייתא about women with a steady, predictable bleeding pattern, and works out which days each one may be with her husband. It counts her 7 days of נדה and 11 days of זיבה for patterns from one-on-one-off up to eight-on-eight-off. In the two-and-two case, the גמרא asks why day 19 is not permitted. רב ששת learns from this that the 'גרגרן' of the משנה is truly forbidden. רב אשי says instead that bleeding on the tenth day of זיבה still needs a clean day. Some patterns make her a זבה גדולה who can never become permitted again, while others repeat in fixed cycles. Finally, the גמרא objects that the eight-and-eight case gives only fourteen permitted days, not fifteen. רב אדא בר יצחק answers that clean days within her נדה week count toward her seven clean days of זיבה. He notes this was once raised as a question, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why call them 'foolish' and not 'mistaken'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word שוטות in רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really fools? They are just mistaken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bothered by a word in the משנה. רבי יהושע called these women 'fools', but they are really just confused about their status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה is someone who lacks basic understanding. These women are not like that. They simply lost track of their cycle. So the word שוטות seems too harsh and does not match the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Foolish women; people who lack understanding
Mistaken women; women who lost track of their cycle and are unsure of their status
They are (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Are they foolish?
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי יהושע's words in the משנה: 'before you fix the foolish women, come fix the smart ones.'

phrases.english: They are mistaken!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge on the wording of רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word שוטות in רבי יהושע's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women who are unsure of their cycle are confused, not foolish, so the word does not fit them.

steps.title: Change the word to 'mistaken'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the text of the משנה to read טועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and fixes the wording. רבי יהושע's statement should say 'mistaken women'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. Only the wording changes. רבי יהושע's point now reads: before you deal with the confused women, deal with the women who know their pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this introduces a correction

phrases.english: Rather, teach: 'mistaken.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה reads שוטות, which suggests the women are foolish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading is טועות, meaning women confused about their cycle.

steps.title: One day bleeding, one day clean: the eighth day is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes a woman who bleeds every other day. She may be with her husband on the eighth day and its night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if one day she is impure and one day she is pure, she may be with her husband on the eighth day, together with its night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to show what the 'smart' women in רבי יהושע's statement look like. These are women with a steady pattern. The first case is a woman who bleeds every other day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She bleeds on days 1, 3, 5 and 7, which are her seven days of נדה. She immerses at the end of the seventh day. Since her pattern says she will not bleed on day 8, she is pure for the eighth day and its night, until she bleeds again on day 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure; here, a day on which she bleeds
Pure; here, a day with no bleeding
She may be intimate with her husband
The eighth day, counted from when she first bled
And its night along with it

steps.confusionAlert: 'Impure day' and 'pure day' here do not describe her legal status for the whole day. They simply mean a day on which she bleeds and a day on which she does not.

phrases.english: As it is taught: one day impure,
and one day pure —
she may engage in intercourse on the eighth day and its night with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing the kind of women רבי יהושע wanted fixed first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who bleeds every other day may be with her husband on the eighth day and its night.

steps.title: Four nights in eighteen days, unless she bleeds in the evening
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Over the eighteen days of נדה and זיבה she has four permitted nights. But if she bleeds at night, only the eighth day is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she also has four nights out of the eighteen days. But if she usually sees blood in the evening, she may be with her husband only on the eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds more permitted times for the same every-other-day woman. It then gives an exception for when her bleeding comes at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eighteen days are 7 days of נדה followed by 11 days of זיבה. She never bleeds two days in a row, so she never becomes a full זבה. After each bleeding during זיבה she waits one clean day (שומרת יום כנגד יום), which leaves four nights that are permitted. If her bleeding comes in the evening, those nights are lost, so only the eighth day remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Nights
Eighteen days: 7 days of נדה plus 11 days of זיבה
In the evening, at night
Only

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the basic structure of 7 days of נדה plus 11 days of זיבה. It also shows how one clean day after a single sighting during זיבה makes her pure again.

phrases.english: And four nights
phrases.notes: These are the nights after days 10, 12, 14 and 16. Each comes after a clean day that follows a sighting.

phrases.english: out of eighteen days.
But if she was seeing in the evening —
she may engage in intercourse only on the eighth alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and the same every-other-day case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She has four permitted nights within the eighteen days. If she bleeds in the evening, only the eighth is permitted.

steps.title: Two days bleeding, two days clean: days 8, 12, 16 and 20
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's second pattern: a woman who bleeds two days and is clean two days may be with her husband on days 8, 12, 16 and 20.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two days she is impure and two days she is pure, she may be with her husband on the eighth, the twelfth, the sixteenth and the twentieth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a second regular pattern: two days of bleeding, then two clean days. It lists the days on which she is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She bleeds on days 1-2 and 5-6, and day 8 is pure after her seven days of נדה. During זיבה she bleeds on days 9-10, which is only two days, so she does not become a full זבה. She keeps day 11 as a clean day, so day 12 is permitted. Day 16 works the same way. Day 20 falls in the new cycle, after a clean day 19, before she has bled again.

keyTerms.meaning: Two days
Twelve, the twelfth day
Sixteen, the sixteenth day
Twenty, the twentieth day

steps.whatToRemember: A woman with a regular pattern can work out her pure days exactly: day 8 always, plus the days that follow a clean day during זיבה. This is what רבי יהושע meant by 'fix the smart women first.'

phrases.english: Two days impure,
and two days pure —
she may engage in intercourse on the eighth, and the twelfth,
and the sixteenth, and the twentieth.
phrases.notes: Day 20 is already in her next cycle. It is permitted because she has not started bleeding again yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טְמֵאִין, וּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא moves from the one-on-one-off pattern to a two-on-two-off pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who bleeds two days and is clean two days may be with her husband on days 8, 12, 16 and 20.

steps.title: Why not day nineteen too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the woman who bleeds two days and is clean two days may not also be with her husband on day 19.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her also be with her husband on the nineteenth day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list of permitted days (8, 12, 16, 20) from the ברייתא. It asks why day 19 is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this pattern she bleeds on days 17 and 18 and is clean on days 19 and 20. Day 18 is the last of the eleven days of זיבה, so day 19 starts a new נדה cycle. It seems she should already be permitted on day 19.

keyTerms.meaning: She may be with her husband
Nineteen (short for תשע עשר)

phrases.english: And let her also be with her husband on the nineteenth!
phrases.notes: תשסר is a shortened way of saying nineteen. The ברייתא only listed days 8, 12, 16 and 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list of permitted days in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's list of permitted days, which leaves out day 19
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The eleven days of זיבה end on day 18, so day 19 should be permitted like any clean day of a new cycle.

steps.title: רב ששת: the 'glutton' is truly forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the ברייתא proves that the 'גרגרן' mentioned in a משנה is actually doing something forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This teaches that the 'glutton' we learned about in the משנה is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. He says day 19 is left out because she bled on day 18, and she must wait out day 19 as a clean day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה calls a husband who does not wait out the clean day after the last day of זיבה a 'גרגרן'. One might think that is only bad manners. The ברייתא's leaving out day 19 shows it is truly forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us (a proof drawn from a source)
A glutton: someone who cannot hold back and wait
Forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a משנה's word of criticism ('glutton') into an actual prohibition.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This teaches,
that the 'glutton' we learned about in a mishna is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 72a, about a husband who does not wait out the day after her last day of bleeding.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a new halachic point from the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Day 19 should be permitted because זיבה has ended.
steps.terutzMaskana: The day after bleeding on the last day of זיבה must still be waited out. Being with her husband on it is forbidden, as the 'גרגרן' משנה hints.

steps.title: רב אשי: the tenth day still needs a clean day
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. Bleeding on the eleventh day needs no clean day, but bleeding on the tenth day does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even though the eleventh day does not need a watched clean day, the tenth day at least does need one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another reason why day 19 is forbidden, without relying on the 'glutton' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day 17 is the tenth day of זיבה, and bleeding on it requires one clean day after it. She could not count day 18 as clean because she bled again, so the clean day moves to day 19. Day 18's bleeding, on the eleventh day, would not need this by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, even though
Watching, keeping one clean day after a day of bleeding
At least, in any case

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say day 19 is forbidden because of day 18. He says it is forbidden because of day 17, the tenth day.
steps.whatToRemember: Day 19 is forbidden for two different reasons. For רב ששת, it is the 'גרגרן' prohibition. For רב אשי, the tenth day's bleeding still needs its clean day.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּחַד עֲשַׂר לָא בָּעֵי שִׁימּוּר,
phrases.english: granted that the eleventh does not need watching,
phrases.notes: The eleventh day of זיבה is day 18 of the full count.

phrases.english: the tenth at least does need watching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: נְהִי דְּחַד עֲשַׂר לָא בָּעֵי שִׁימּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to step 6, so no proof is needed about the 'גרגרן'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for the same result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Day 19 must be forbidden only because of the 'גרגרן' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bleeding on day 17, the tenth day of זיבה, needs a clean day. Since day 18 was not clean, she must keep day 19 clean.

steps.title: Three days bleeding, three days clean
steps.stepSummary: A woman who bleeds three days and is clean three days may be with her husband on two days, and never again after that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three days impure and three days pure: she may be with her husband for two days, and after that never again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a third pattern: three days of bleeding, then three clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Days 8 and 9 are bleeding days early in זיבה, so she can be with her husband on days 11 and 12. After that she bleeds three days in a row during זיבה and becomes a זבה גדולה. She then needs seven clean days, which this pattern never gives her.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure (days she bleeds)
Pure (clean days)
And after that she may never again be with her husband

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים טְמֵאִין וּשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין,
phrases.english: Three days impure and three days pure:
she may be with her husband for two days,
and after that she may never again be with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים טְמֵאִין וּשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list of patterns after the side discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a three-and-three pattern she is permitted only on days 11 and 12. After that she is a זבה גדולה forever.

steps.title: Four days bleeding, four days clean
steps.stepSummary: A woman who bleeds four days and is clean four days may be with her husband on one day only, and never again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four days impure and four days pure: she may be with her husband for one day, and after that never again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its next pattern: four days of bleeding, then four clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She bleeds days 1 to 4 and is clean days 5 to 8. She is only permitted on day 8, after her נדה purification. Days 9 to 12 are three or more days of bleeding in זיבה, which make her a זבה גדולה. She can never collect seven clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who bled three days in a row during זיבה and needs seven clean days
One day

steps.whatToRemember: In the 3/3 and 4/4 patterns, her bleeding during זיבה lasts three days or more. That makes her a זבה גדולה, and since she never gets seven clean days in a row, she is never permitted again.

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים טְמֵאִים, וְאַרְבָּעָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין —
phrases.english: Four days impure and four days pure:
she may be with her husband for one day,
phrases.notes: This is day 8, the last of her first four clean days.

phrases.english: and after that she may never again be with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים טְמֵאִים, וְאַרְבָּעָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the next pattern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a four-and-four pattern she is permitted only on day 8. After that she is a זבה גדולה forever.

steps.title: Five days bleeding, five days clean
steps.stepSummary: A woman who bleeds five days and is clean five days may be with her husband for three days, and never again after that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has five days of bleeding and then five clean days, she may be with her husband for three days, and after that never again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of fixed patterns. Now it gives the case of a woman who bleeds five days and then is clean five days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Days 1-7 are her days of נדה, so the clean days 8, 9 and 10 are permitted. Her next bleeding, on days 11-15, falls in her days of זיבה. Three or more days of bleeding there makes her a זבה גדולה, who needs seven clean days in a row. Since she only ever gets five clean days, she can never become pure again.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure days, the days she sees blood
Pure days, the days she sees no blood
After that she may never again be with her husband
A woman who bleeds three days in a row during her days of זיבה; she needs seven clean days in a row

phrases.english: Five days impure,
and five days pure —
she may be with her husband three days,
phrases.notes: These are days 8, 9 and 10, after her seven days of נדה end.

phrases.english: and then she may never again be with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה יָמִים טְמֵאִים, וַחֲמִשָּׁה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of fixed patterns after the 3/3 and 4/4 cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 5 bleeding / 5 clean: permitted three days, then never again.

steps.title: Six days bleeding, six days clean
steps.stepSummary: A woman who bleeds six days and is clean six days may be with her husband for five days, and never again after that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has six days of bleeding and then six clean days, she may be with her husband for five days, and after that never again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pattern in the list: six days of bleeding followed by six clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her seven days of נדה cover days 1-7, so the clean days 8-12 (five days) are permitted. Her next bleeding, on days 13-18, falls in her days of זיבה and makes her a זבה גדולה. With only six clean days in each cycle, she never reaches the seven clean days she needs.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven days from the start of bleeding that count as נדה
The eleven days after the days of נדה, when bleeding can make her a זבה
Seven clean days in a row, which a זבה גדולה must count before she becomes pure

phrases.english: Six days impure,
and six days pure —
she may be with her husband five days,
phrases.notes: Days 8 through 12. Day 7 is clean, but it is still one of her days of נדה.

phrases.english: and then she may never again be with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשָּׁה יָמִים טְמֵאִין, וְשִׁשָּׁה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the same list, one day longer each way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 6 bleeding / 6 clean: permitted five days, then never again.

steps.title: Seven days bleeding, seven days clean
steps.stepSummary: A woman who bleeds seven days and is clean seven days may be with her husband a quarter of her days: seven out of every twenty-eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has seven days of bleeding and then seven clean days, she may be with her husband a quarter of her days, seven out of every twenty-eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the 7/7 pattern. Unlike the earlier cases, here she does not become forbidden forever. Instead she follows a repeating 28-day cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Days 1-7 are נדה, and days 8-14 are clean and permitted. Days 15-21 fall in her days of זיבה and make her a זבה גדולה, so days 22-28 serve as her seven clean days. On day 29 a fresh cycle of נדה starts, so she is permitted only seven of every 28 days.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of her days
Out of
Twenty-eight

steps.confusionAlert: The clean days 22-28 are not permitted days. They only count as her seven clean days for the זיבה, so she becomes pure at their end, just as a new cycle of bleeding begins.

phrases.english: Seven days impure,
and seven days pure —
she may be with her husband a quarter of her days,
out of twenty-eight days.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְעָה יָמִים טְמֵאִין, וְשִׁבְעָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the list; here the pattern turns into a repeating cycle instead of ending forever.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 7 bleeding / 7 clean: permitted seven out of every 28 days.

steps.title: Eight days bleeding, eight days clean
steps.stepSummary: A woman who bleeds eight days and is clean eight days may be with her husband fifteen days out of every forty-eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has eight days of bleeding and then eight clean days, she may be with her husband fifteen days out of every forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last pattern in this list, 8/8, which repeats in a 48-day cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day 8 of bleeding falls in her days of זיבה, so she is a זבה קטנה and keeps one clean day. Then she has seven permitted days. The next set again mixes זיבה days and a new cycle of נדה, which gives her seven more permitted days. Later she becomes a זבה גדולה, and after her seven clean days one more day is left, for a total of 15.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who bleeds one or two days during her days of זיבה
Keeping one clean day for each day of bleeding, the rule for a זבה קטנה
Forty-eight

phrases.english: Eight days impure,
and eight days pure —
she may be with her husband fifteen days
out of forty-eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים טְמֵאִין, וּשְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final and most complicated case in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 8 bleeding / 8 clean: permitted fifteen out of every 48 days.

steps.title: The permitted days are only fourteen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that in the 8/8 case the permitted days add up to only fourteen, not fifteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count it just gave for the 8/8 case and says it should be fourteen days, not fifteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes she cannot count her seven clean days of זיבה on days that are fit to be her days of נדה. If so, her seven clean days start later and do not finish before her next bleeding on day 49. That means the last day (day 48) is not permitted, which leaves only fourteen days.

keyTerms.meaning: These
Fourteen
They are

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this challenge will show whether clean days of זיבה may be counted during days that could be days of נדה.

phrases.english: But these are fourteen!
phrases.notes: He means the permitted days in the 8/8 case add up to fourteen, not the fifteen just stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the number given in the 8/8 case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 8/8 woman is permitted fifteen of every 48 days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If clean days of זיבה cannot be counted on days fit for נדה, her seven clean days are not finished before the next bleeding on day 49. Day 48 is then forbidden, so only fourteen days are permitted.

steps.title: Clean days within the נדה week count toward the זיבה count
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר יצחק explains the fifteen. Her נדה days on which she sees no blood still count toward her seven clean days of זיבה. The גמרא then points to an earlier question about this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר יצחק said: This teaches that the days of her נדה week on which she does not see blood count toward the counting of her זיבה clean days. For this was asked as a question:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר יצחק answers the 'only fourteen' objection by drawing a rule out of the 8/8 case. He then says this rule was once raised as a question, which the גמרא brings at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed she can start counting her seven clean days of זיבה only after her נדה week ends. רב אדא says no: clean days that fall inside the נדה week already count toward the seven. That lets her finish her count sooner, which adds the missing day and brings the total to fifteen.

keyTerms.meaning: Her נדה days: the fixed seven-day נדה week that starts with her period
The counting of seven clean days that a זבה needs before she becomes טהורה
'Go up' / count toward a total
'It was asked of them': a question raised in the בית מדרש

steps.whatToRemember: The fifteen in the 8/8 case works only if clean days inside the נדה week count toward the seven clean days of זיבה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of days. The נדה days are a fixed seven-day week no matter what. The seven clean days are a count a זבה must finish without any blood. The question is whether one day can serve both purposes at once.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the step from a math correction into a real rule about how the נדה and זבה counts overlap. The גמרא will now look at whether that rule was in doubt.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Yitzchak said:
This is to say,
phrases.notes: He means: the fifteen in the 8/8 case teaches us the following rule.

phrases.english: her נדה days on which she does not see blood
count toward the counting of her זיבה clean days,
for it was asked of them:
phrases.notes: The actual question comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אדא בר יצחק זאת אומרת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 15 by bringing in a rule that makes the count reach fifteen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a new rule out of the case, which fixes the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven clean days of זיבה can only be counted after the נדה week ends, so the total reaches only fourteen.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clean days inside the נדה week already count toward the seven clean days, which adds a day and gives fifteen.
